claim: Antibody array screening of FACS-defined stromal vascular fraction (SVF) perivascular cells identified several novel cell surface antigens, including CD107a, enriched within subpopulations of human adventicytes and pericytes.
source: Here, antibody array screening of FACS-defined stromal vascular fraction (SVF) perivascular cells identified several novel cell surface antigens, including CD107a, enriched within subpopulations of human adventicytes and pericytes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data from Lyoplate analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: CD107a is a member of a family of structurally related type one membrane proteins predominantly expressed in lysosomes and other intracellular vesicles.
source: CD107a (lysosome-associated membrane protein-1, LAMP1) is a member of a family of structurally related type one membrane proteins predominantly expressed in lysosomes and other intracellular vesicles (Carlsson et al., 1988; de Saint-Vis et al., 1998; Defays et al., 2011; Ramprasad et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: CD107a expression on the cell surface results from trafficking of nascent protein to the plasma membrane as well as the fusion of late endosomes and lysosomes to the cell membrane.
source: CD107a is far less frequently expressed on the cell surface, which is the result of both trafficking of nascent protein to the plasma membrane as well as the fusion of late endosomes and lysosomes to the cell membrane (Akasaki et al., 1993; Dell'Angelica et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In inflammatory cells, surface CD107a reflects the state of activation.
source: In inflammatory cells, surface CD107a reflects the state of activation (Janvier and Bonifacino, 2005) and has been implicated in cell adhesion (Kannan et al., 1996; Min et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD107a has been implicated in cell adhesion.
source: In inflammatory cells, surface CD107a reflects the state of activation (Janvier and Bonifacino, 2005) and has been implicated in cell adhesion (Kannan et al., 1996; Min et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD107a has been described in intracellular vesicles in both osteoblasts and adipocytes.
source: In separate reports, CD107a has been described in intracellular vesicles in both osteoblasts and adipocytes (Bandeira et al., 2018; Solberg et al., 2015), yet beyond this, essentially nothing is known regarding CD107a in mesenchymal stem cell fate or differentiation decisions.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD107ahigh cells represent an adipocyte precursor cell.
source: CD107ahigh cells represent an adipocyte precursor cell, while CD107alow cells represent progenitors with increased osteoblast potential.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro differentiation assays shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: CD107alow cells represent progenitors with increased osteoblast potential.
source: CD107ahigh cells represent an adipocyte precursor cell, while CD107alow cells represent progenitors with increased osteoblast potential.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro differentiation assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: CD107a trafficking to the cell surface occurs during early adipocyte differentiation.
source: CD107a trafficking to the cell surface was observed to occur during early adipocyte differentiation – results confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from mouse and human adipose tissues.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by immunocytochemistry and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3H-L.

claim: CD107alow cells robustly induce bone formation in an intramuscular ectopic ossicle assay in mice.
source: Upon transplantation into immunocompromised rodents, CD107alow cells robustly induce bone formation, both in an intramuscular ectopic ossicle assay in mice and a lumbar spine fusion rat model.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by μCT and histological data shown in Figure 5.

claim: CD107alow cells robustly induce bone formation in a lumbar spine fusion rat model.
source: Upon transplantation into immunocompromised rodents, CD107alow cells robustly induce bone formation, both in an intramuscular ectopic ossicle assay in mice and a lumbar spine fusion rat model.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by μCT and histological data shown in Figure 6.

claim: CD107a expression was 32% among adventitial cells (CD34+CD146-CD45-CD31- cells).
source: Novel markers to divide perivascular progenitors ranged broadly, including the endolysosomal protein CD107a (32% and 82% expression among adventicytes and pericytes, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Lyoplate analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: CD107a expression was 82% among pericytes (CD146+CD34-CD45-CD31- cells).
source: Novel markers to divide perivascular progenitors ranged broadly, including the endolysosomal protein CD107a (32% and 82% expression among adventicytes and pericytes, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Lyoplate analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: CD107b was expressed on 13% of adventitial cells and 46% of pericytes.
source: Another endolysosomal protein, CD107b, was also present on each perivascular cell fraction (13% and 46% expressing adventicytes and pericytes, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Lyoplate analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: CD90 (Thy-1) is highly expressed among both adventicytes and pericytes.
source: Several markers were confirmed to be highly expressed among both adventicytes and pericytes, including, for example, the progenitor cell and MSC marker CD90 (Thy-1) and the perivascular cell antigen CD140b (PDGFRβ).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Lyoplate analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: CD140b (PDGFRβ) is highly expressed among both adventicytes and pericytes.
source: Several markers were confirmed to be highly expressed among both adventicytes and pericytes, including, for example, the progenitor cell and MSC marker CD90 (Thy-1) and the perivascular cell antigen CD140b (PDGFRβ).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Lyoplate analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: LAMP1 gene expression was confirmed in WAT-derived pericytes with mean FPKM values of 9.576.
source: Using WAT-derived pericytes (n = 3 samples, GEO dataset: GSE125545) or adventitial perivascular stem cells (n = 3 samples, GEO dataset: GSE130086) (Xu et al., 2019), high expression of the LAMP1 gene was confirmed (mean FPKM values of 9.576 and 9.619, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by transcriptomics data from GEO datasets.

claim: LAMP1 gene expression was confirmed in adventitial perivascular stem cells with mean FPKM values of 9.619.
source: Using WAT-derived pericytes (n = 3 samples, GEO dataset: GSE125545) or adventitial perivascular stem cells (n = 3 samples, GEO dataset: GSE130086) (Xu et al., 2019), high expression of the LAMP1 gene was confirmed (mean FPKM values of 9.576 and 9.619, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by transcriptomics data from GEO datasets.

claim: CD107a immunoreactivity was found most frequently within the outermost layers of larger arteries and veins in subcutaneous WAT.
source: CD107a immunoreactivity was found most frequently within the outermost layers of larger arteries (Figure 1B) and veins (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: The outer tunica adventitia of arteries showed a high frequency of CD107a+CD34+ cells.
source: Within arteries, the outer tunica adventitia showed a high frequency of CD107a+CD34+ cells (Figure 1B1), while the inner adventitia showed predominantly CD107a-CD34+ cells (Figure 1B2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1B1.

claim: The inner adventitia of arteries showed predominantly CD107a-CD34+ cells.
source: Within arteries, the outer tunica adventitia showed a high frequency of CD107a+CD34+ cells (Figure 1B1), while the inner adventitia showed predominantly CD107a-CD34+ cells (Figure 1B2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1B2.

claim: The smooth muscle media of arteries largely did not show CD107a immunoreactivity.
source: The smooth muscle media largely did not show CD107a immunoreactivity (Figure 1B3), which was confirmed by dual immunohistochemistry for CD107a and αSMA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1B3 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD107a immunoreactive adventitial cells showed little overlap with Gli1 expression.
source: Co-expression with the recently described adventitial marker Gli1 was assessed (Kramann et al., 2016), which showed little overlap with CD107a immunoreactive adventitial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Capillaries within WAT showed some CD107a immunoreactive pericytes, which co-expressed CD146 but not CD31, and were present in an abluminal location.
source: Capillaries within WAT showed some CD107a immunoreactive pericytes, which co-expressed CD146 but not CD31, and were present in an abluminal location (Figure 1E, appearing yellow).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1E.

claim: CD107a immunoreactivity within the perivascular mesenchymal niche was confirmed across pericardial, perigonadal, perirenal, and omental human fat depots.
source: CD107a immunoreactivity within the perivascular mesenchymal niche was confirmed across other AT depots, including pericardial, perigonadal, perirenal, and omental human fat (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, n = 3 samples per depot).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mean frequency of CD107alow mesenchymal cells represented 33.75% of viable SVF.
source: Mean frequency of CD107alow mesenchymal cells represented 33.75% of viable SVF, while mean frequency of CD107ahigh mesenchymal cells represented 5.20% (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Mean frequency of CD107ahigh mesenchymal cells represented 5.20% of viable SVF.
source: Mean frequency of CD107alow mesenchymal cells represented 33.75% of viable SVF, while mean frequency of CD107ahigh mesenchymal cells represented 5.20% (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: CD34+ and CD146+ cells were identified in both CD107alow and CD107ahigh cell fractions.
source: Concordant with histological observations, CD34+ and CD146+ cells were identified in both CD107alow and CD107ahigh cell fractions (Figure 1H,I, mean frequencies reported in Supplementary file 2, 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1H, 1I, and Supplementary files 2 and 3.

claim: CD105 expression was disproportionately present within CD107ahigh mesenchymal cells (mean frequency 0.44% and 8.12% among CD107alow and CD107ahigh cells, respectively).
source: CD105 expression was disproportionately present within CD107ahigh mesenchymal cells (mean frequency 0.44% and 8.12% among CD107alow and CD107ahigh cells, respectively).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Supplementary file 4 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: CD107alow cells demonstrated a higher proliferative rate in comparison to CD107ahigh cells.
source: CD107alow cells demonstrated a higher proliferative rate in comparison to CD107ahigh cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by MTS assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Among freshly isolated cells, the vast majority of colony forming units-fibroblast (CFU-F) was identified within the CD107alow cell fraction.
source: Among freshly isolated cells, the vast majority of colony forming units-fibroblast (CFU-F) was identified within the CD107alow cell fraction (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by CFU-F assay data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: Among equivalent cells at passage 4, an enrichment in CFU-F was still observed in CD107alow cells.
source: Among equivalent cells at passage 4, an enrichment in CFU-F was still observed in CD107alow cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by CFU-F assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: CFU-OB assays performed in growth medium showed alkaline phosphatase (ALP)+ colonies among CD107alow cells only.
source: CFU-OB assays performed in growth medium showed alkaline phosphatase (ALP)+ colonies among CD107alow cells only (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by CFU-OB assay data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: CFU-OB assays performed in osteogenic differentiation medium showed an enrichment in CFU-OB among CD107alow cells.
source: The same experiment performed in osteogenic differentiation medium showed an enrichment in CFU-OB among CD107alow cells (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by CFU-OB assay data shown in Figure 2G and 2H.

claim: ALP staining and quantification demonstrated an enrichment among CD107alow cells.
source: ALP staining and quantification demonstrated an enrichment among CD107alow cells (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ALP staining data shown in Figure 2I and 2J.

claim: Bone nodule formation was increased in CD107alow cells as compared to CD107ahigh counterparts.
source: Bone nodule formation was likewise increased in CD107alow cells as compared to CD107ahigh counterparts (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Alizarin red staining data shown in Figure 2K and 2L.

claim: Osteogenic gene expression across timepoints of differentiation showed an enrichment for RUNX2, ALPL, and osteopontin (SPP1) in CD107alow cells.
source: Osteogenic gene expression across timepoints of differentiation likewise showed an enrichment for RUNX2 (Runt related transcription factor 2), ALPL, and osteopontin (SPP1) (Figure 2M–O).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2M-O.

claim: Among freshly isolated cells, essentially all CFU-adipocyte (CFU-AD) were found within the CD107ahigh cell population.
source: Among freshly isolated cells, essentially all CFU-adipocyte (CFU-AD) were found within the CD107ahigh cell population (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by CFU-AD assay data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Oil red O staining was significantly more abundant among the CD107ahigh cells.
source: Oil red O staining was significantly more abundant among the CD107ahigh cells (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Oil red O staining data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: All adipogenic marker gene transcripts showed significant enrichment among CD107ahigh cells in comparison to CD107alow counterparts, including PPARG, LPL, and FABP4.
source: All marker gene transcripts showed significant enrichment among CD107ahigh cells in comparison to CD107alow counterparts, including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG), lipoprotein lipase (LPL), and fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: After 3 d exposure to adipogenic conditions, a 12.03 fold increase in CD107a immunostaining intensity was noted in unpurified ASCs.
source: After 3 d exposure to adipogenic conditions, a 12.03 fold increase in immunostaining intensity and a 253.5% increase in the number of CD107ahigh cells were noted.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 3H and 3I.

claim: After 3 d exposure to adipogenic conditions, a 253.5% increase in the number of CD107ahigh cells was noted in unpurified ASCs.
source: After 3 d exposure to adipogenic conditions, a 12.03 fold increase in immunostaining intensity and a 253.5% increase in the number of CD107ahigh cells were noted.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Flow cytometry across several human cell types confirmed an increase in CD107ahigh cell frequency during adipogenic differentiation, including FACS-purified perivascular stem cells (PSCs) and culture-defined human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) (188.1–455.4% increase in CD107ahigh cell frequency).
source: Flow cytometry across several other human cell types confirmed this finding, including FACS-purified perivascular stem cells (PSCs) (Figure 3K) and culture-defined human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) (Figure 3L) (188.1–455.4% increase in CD107ahigh cell frequency).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3K and 3L.

claim: Parallel experiments under osteogenic differentiation conditions found no significant increase in CD107a staining intensity.
source: Parallel experiments were performed under osteogenic differentiation conditions, which found no significant increase in CD107a staining intensity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Treatment with Vac-1 significantly decreased the frequency of CD107ahigh ASCs, and prevented an increase of cell surface CD107a by adipogenic conditions.
source: Treatment with Vac-1 significantly decreased the frequency of CD107ahigh ASCs, and prevented an increase of cell surface CD107a by adipogenic conditions (Figure 3M,N).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunocytochemistry and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3M and 3N.

claim: KEGG terms for exocytosis showed enrichment within early and middle progenitor cells in human AT-derived cells.
source: KEGG terms for exocytosis showed enrichment within early and middle progenitor cells, as visualized by heatmaps across pseudotime (Figure 3R) and normalized expression of overall exocytosis gene activation (Figure 3S).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3R and 3S.

claim: Normalized exocytosis gene activation scores were enriched within early Dpp4-expressing progenitor cells in comparison to more mature Dlk1-expressing pre-adipocytes in mouse subcutaneous WAT.
source: Normalized exocytosis gene activation scores were again enriched within early Dpp4-expressing progenitor cells in comparison to more mature Dlk1-expressing pre-adipocytes.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D and 3E.

claim: SiRNA-mediated KD of LAMP1 (encoding CD107a) showed no appreciable effect on the osteogenic differentiation of human ASCs.
source: SiRNA-mediated KD of LAMP1 (encoding CD107a) showed no appreciable effect on the osteogenic differentiation of human ASCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Alizarin red staining and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A-F.

claim: During adipogenesis, LAMP1 KD ASCs and CD107alow adventicytes showed a modest increase in lipid droplet accumulation.
source: During adipogenesis, LAMP1 KD ASCs and CD107alow adventicytes showed a modest increase in lipid droplet accumulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4G,K,L,P,Q) and likewise a modest increase in expression of adipogenic marker genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 4H–J,M–O).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Oil red O staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4G, K, L, P, and Q.

claim: During adipogenesis, LAMP1 KD ASCs and CD107alow adventicytes showed a modest increase in expression of adipogenic marker genes.
source: During adipogenesis, LAMP1 KD ASCs and CD107alow adventicytes showed a modest increase in lipid droplet accumulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4G,K,L,P,Q) and likewise a modest increase in expression of adipogenic marker genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 4H–J,M–O).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4H-J and M-O.

claim: The high adipogenic differentiation potential of CD107ahigh cells was not significantly altered with LAMP1 KD.
source: The high adipogenic differentiation potential of CD107ahigh cells was not significantly altered with LAMP1 KD (Figure 3—figure supplement 4P,Q).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Oil red O staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4P and Q.

claim: Clear separation between gene expression profiles was observed when comparing CD107alow with CD107ahigh stromal cells, as assessed by principal component analysis.
source: Clear separation between gene expression profiles was observed when comparing CD107alow with CD107ahigh stromal cells, as assessed by principal component analysis (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Endothelial and inflammatory marker genes were rarely or not expressed among CD107alow and CD107ahigh stromal cells.
source: Further confirming our FACS purification, endothelial and inflammatory marker genes were rarely or not expressed among CD107alow and CD107ahigh stromal cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcripts of MYC, LEPR, MCAM, and PDGFRA were enriched among CD107alow cells.
source: Transcripts of MYC, LEPR (Leptin receptor), MCAM (CD146), and PDGFRA (Platelet-derived growth factor receptor α) while expressed across all samples were enriched among CD107alow cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NES, THY1, PDGFRB and TBX18 were expressed across all samples, but more highly among CD107ahigh cells.
source: Likewise, NES (Nestin), THY1 (CD90), PDGFRB (Platelet-derived growth factor receptor β) and TBX18 (T-Box transcription factor 18) were expressed across all samples, but more highly among CD107ahigh cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Genes associated with adipogenic differentiation were highly expressed among CD107ahigh stromal cells, such as FABP4, LPL, PPARGC1A, and CEBPA.
source: Consistent with in vitro differentiation potential, genes associated with adipogenic differentiation were highly expressed among CD107ahigh stromal cells, such as FABP4 (Fatty acid-binding protein 4), LPL (Lipoprotein lipase), PPARGC1A (PPARG coactivator 1 α), and CEBPA (CCAAT enhancer binding protein α).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Negative regulators of adipogenesis were increased among CD107alow stromal cells, such as KLF2, KLF3, SIRT1, and DDIT3.
source: In addition, negative regulators of adipogenesis were increased among CD107alow stromal cells, such as KLF2 (Krüppel-like factor 2), KLF3, SIRT1 (Sirtuin 1), and DDIT3 (DNA Damage Inducible Transcript 3) (Figure 4C; Banerjee et al., 2003; Pereira et al., 2004; Sue et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4C and citations to prior literature.

claim: IPA showed that the activated pathways in CD107ahigh stromal cells are associated with the positive regulation of adipogenesis, including white adipose tissue browning pathway and Sirtuin signaling (Z scores 1.342 and 1.387).
source: QIAGEN Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) showed that the activated pathways in CD107ahigh stromal cells are associated with the positive regulation of adipogenesis, including, for example, white adipose tissue browning pathway and Sirtuin signaling (Z scores 1.342 and 1.387; CD107ahigh compared with CD107alow stromal cells; Figure 4D; Kurylowicz, 2019).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by IPA data shown in Figure 4D and a citation to prior literature.

claim: Upregulated signaling pathways in CD107alow stromal cells included Wnt/β-catenin signaling as well as pathways associated with cellular respiration and metabolism, including Oxidative Phosphorylation and Glutathione metabolism (Z scores −1).
source: Conversely, upregulated signaling pathways in CD107alow stromal cells included Wnt/β-catenin signaling as well as pathways associated with cellular respiration and metabolism, including Oxidative Phosphorylation and Glutathione metabolism (Z scores −1; CD107ahigh compared with CD107alow stromal cells; Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by IPA data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Highly enriched GO terms among CD107alow stromal cells were likewise found to be enriched among DPP4+ cell fractions during 'early' pseudotime.
source: Highly enriched GO terms among CD107alow stromal cells were likewise found to be enriched among DPP4+ cell fractions during 'early' pseudotime (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by pathway analysis data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: GO terms enriched within CD107ahigh stromal cells were likewise enriched among GGT5+ cell fractions within 'late' pseudotime.
source: Conversely, GO terms enriched within CD107ahigh stromal cells were likewise enriched among GGT5+ cell fractions within 'late' pseudotime (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by pathway analysis data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Quantitative μCT analysis demonstrated a significant increase in bone volume (BV, 97.7% increase), fractional bone volume (BV/TV, 73.4% increase), and bone surfaces (BS, 91.4% increase) among CD107alow as compared to CD107ahigh implants.
source: Quantitative μCT analysis demonstrated a significant increase in bone volume (BV, 97.7% increase), fractional bone volume (BV/TV, 73.4% increase), and bone surfaces (BS, 91.4% increase) among CD107alow as compared to CD107ahigh implants (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by μCT data shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: CD107ahigh cells exhibited bone-forming potential in comparison to acellular control (292.1–473.3% increase in μCT quantitative metrics).
source: Albeit to a lesser degree, CD107ahigh cells did exhibit bone-forming potential in comparison to acellular control (292.1–473.3% increase in μCT quantitative metrics, Figure 5B–D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by μCT data shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: Bone histomorphometric analysis demonstrated significantly increased osteoblast number (N.Ob, 237.5% increase), increased osteoblast number per bone surface (N.Ob/BS, 232.5% increase), and osteocyte number (N.Ot, 460.3% increase) among CD107alow implants compared to CD107ahigh implants.
source: Bone histomorphometric analysis confirmed these observations, demonstrating significantly increased osteoblast number (N.Ob, 237.5% increase), increased osteoblast number per bone surface (N.Ob/BS, 232.5% increase), and osteocyte number (N.Ot, 460.3% increase) (Figure 5F–H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: ALP staining and semi-quantitative analysis confirmed an overall increase in serial sections of CD107alow treated implants (14.3% increase among CD107alow implant sites).
source: ALP staining and semi-quantitative analysis confirmed an overall increase in serial sections of CD107alow treated implants (Figure 5I,J, 14.3% increase among CD107alow implant sites).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ALP staining data shown in Figure 5I and 5J.

claim: Enrichment in the terminal osteogenic differentiation marker osteocalcin (OCN) was confirmed among CD107alow implants (345.3% increase among CD107alow implant sites).
source: Enrichment in the terminal osteogenic differentiation marker osteocalcin (OCN) was also confirmed among CD107alow implants, shown by immunostaining and semi-quantitative analysis (Figure 5K,L, 345.3% increase among CD107alow implant sites).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5K and 5L.

claim: Detection of human nuclear antigen (HNA) among implant sites confirmed the persistence of human cells across both groups, which were overall similar in frequency.
source: Detection of human nuclear antigen (HNA) among implant sites confirmed the persistence of human cells across both groups, which were overall similar in frequency (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Progressive increase in density of the implant sites was confirmed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-based quantification, with a gradual and significant increase in CD107alow treated spinal implants in comparison to either CD107ahigh treated cells or control.
source: Progressive increase in density of the implant sites was confirmed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-based quantification, with a gradual and significant increase in CD107alow treated spinal implants in comparison to either CD107ahigh treated cells or control (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by DXA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: After 8 weeks acellular control-treated animals showed 14.3% fusion (1/7 animals).
source: Consistent with prior studies (Chung et al., 2014), after 8 weeks acellular control-treated animals showed 14.3% fusion (1/7 animals).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by manual palpation data shown in Figure 6B and a citation to prior literature.

claim: Analyses performed after 8 weeks demonstrated 62.5% spine fusion among CD107alow treated animals (6/8 animals).
source: Analyses performed after 8 weeks demonstrated 62.5% spine fusion among CD107alow treated animals (6/8 animals).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by manual palpation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: CD107ahigh treated animals showed 37.5% fusion (3/8 animals).
source: In comparison, CD107ahigh treated animals showed 37.5% fusion (3/8 animals).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by manual palpation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Quantitative μCT analysis demonstrated a significant increase in bone volume (BV), fractional bone volume (BV/TV), and bone surfaces (BS) among CD107alow implant sites in comparison to acellular control (58.6–80.7% increase across μCT metrics).
source: Quantitative μCT analysis demonstrated a significant increase in bone volume (BV), fractional bone volume (BV/TV), and bone surfaces (BS) among CD107alow implant sites in comparison to acellular control (Figure 6D–F, 58.6–80.7% increase across μCT metrics).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by μCT data shown in Figure 6D-F.

claim: CD107ahigh spine fusion segments demonstrate no statistically significant change in μCT assessments in comparison to acellular control (15.3–25.2% change in comparison to acellular control).
source: In contrast, CD107ahigh spine fusion segments demonstrate no statistically significant change in μCT assessments in comparison to acellular control (Figure 6D–F, 15.3–25.2% change in comparison to acellular control).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by μCT data shown in Figure 6D-F.

claim: Bone histomorphometric analysis demonstrated significantly increased osteoblast number (172.2% increase among CD107alow implant sites in comparison to CD107ahigh implant sites), increased osteoblast number per bone surface (183.5% increase), and osteocyte number (357.1% increase) in spine fusion segments.
source: Bone histomorphometric analysis confirmed these observations, demonstrating significantly increased osteoblast number (172.2% increase among CD107alow implant sites in comparison to CD107ahigh implant sites), increased osteoblast number per bone surface (183.5% increase), and osteocyte number (357.1% increase) (Figure 6H–J).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 6H-J.

claim: Microvascular pericytes demonstrate progenitor cell attributes.
source: Microvascular pericytes, although less frequent in absolute numbers, also demonstrate progenitor cell attributes (Chen et al., 2013; Crisan et al., 2009; Crisan et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Perivascular cells, including those found within the tunica adventitia (adventitial cells or adventicytes), demonstrate more phenotypic and functional diversity than previously understood.
source: With several recent studies from our group in human (Ding et al., 2019; Hardy et al., 2017) and mouse WAT (Wang et al., 2020), it is clear that perivascular cells, including those found within the tunica adventitia (adventitial cells or adventicytes), demonstrate more phenotypic and functional diversity than previously understood.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature from the authors' group.

claim: The bulk of WAT-resident perivascular cells with mesenchymal progenitor cell attributes reside in the tunica adventitia – the outer collagen-rich sheath of blood vessels.
source: The bulk of WAT-resident perivascular cells with mesenchymal progenitor cell attributes reside in the tunica adventitia – the outer collagen-rich sheath of blood vessels (Corselli et al., 2012; James et al., 2012a; West et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The ability of human WAT-resident perivascular cells to differentiate into bone-forming osteoblasts and incite or participate in bone repair is well known.
source: The ability of human WAT-resident perivascular cells to differentiate into bone-forming osteoblasts and incite or participate in bone repair is also well known (Askarinam et al., 2013; Chung et al., 2014; James et al., 2012a; James et al., 2012b; James et al., 2012c; Lee et al., 2015; Meyers et al., 2018b; Tawonsawatruk et al., 2016) (see (James et al., 2017; James and Péault, 2019) for reviews).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: CD107alow cells are precursors of CD107ahigh cells.
source: RNA sequencing also suggested that CD107alow cells are precursors of CD107ahigh cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA sequencing and pathway analysis data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both CD107alow and CD107ahigh subpopulations of human SVF house multipotent mesenchymal cells.
source: Thus, CD107alow and CD107ahigh subpopulations of human SVF both house multipotent mesenchymal cells, but with considerably divergent osteoblastic and adipocytic differentiation potentials.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by chondrogenic differentiation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD107alow and CD107ahigh cell populations both demonstrated a progressive increase in cartilage associated gene expression after 7 d in chondrogenic differentiation conditions.
source: Here, both cell populations demonstrated a progressive increase in cartilage associated gene expression after 7 d in chondrogenic differentiation conditions.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No significant differences in cartilage gene expression were observed between CD107alow and CD107ahigh cell fractions.
source: No significant differences in cartilage gene expression were observed between CD107alow and CD107ahigh cell fractions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Alcian blue stained sections of micromass cultures at 21 d of differentiation showed a similar appearance between CD107alow and CD107ahigh cells.
source: Alcian blue stained sections of micromass cultures at 21 d of differentiation likewise showed a similar appearance between CD107alow and CD107ahigh cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Alcian blue staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CD107alow cells likely represent a more progenitor cell, while CD107ahigh cells are a more mature, differentiated cell population.
source: Thus, CD107alow cells likely represent a more progenitor cell, while CD107ahigh cells are a more mature, differentiated cell population.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by in vitro differentiation data and RNA sequencing data.

claim: Similar results are found in the hematopoietic system, where the most primitive hematopoietic stem cells are Thy-1low, whereas Thy-1high cells belong to a well-defined blood cell lineage.
source: Similar results are found in the hematopoietic system, where the most primitive hematopoietic stem cells are Thy-1low, whereas Thy-1high cells belong to a well-defined blood cell lineage (Spangrude et al., 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Subsets of mouse pericytes are known, in contexts of experimental disease or injury, to give rise in situ to white adipocytes, follicular dendritic cells, myoblasts, and myofibroblasts.
source: While subsets of mouse pericytes are known, in contexts of experimental disease or injury, to give rise in situ to white adipocytes, follicular dendritic cells, myoblasts, and myofibroblasts (Dellavalle et al., 2011; Dulauroy et al., 2012; Krautler et al., 2012; Murray et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2008), the osteogenic and chondrogenic potentials present in these microvascular cells are unlikely to be ever used in the turnover and repair of soft tissues.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A contribution to blood vessel pathologic remodeling of perivascular presumptive MSCs has been recognized, as osteoblast and smooth muscle cell forerunners for calcific arteriosclerosis and atherosclerosis, respectively.
source: On the other hand, a contribution to blood vessel pathologic remodeling of perivascular presumptive MSCs has been recognized, as osteoblast and smooth muscle cell forerunners for calcific arteriosclerosis and atherosclerosis, respectively (Kramann et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CD10 expression marks a subset of human adipose tissue adventitial cells with higher bone-forming potential.
source: For instance, CD10 expression marks a subset of human adipose tissue adventitial cells with higher bone-forming potential (Ding et al., 2019), and the highest calcification potential is attributed to mouse adventitial cells co-expressing CD34 and PDGFRα (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The highest calcification potential is attributed to mouse adventitial cells co-expressing CD34 and PDGFRα.
source: For instance, CD10 expression marks a subset of human adipose tissue adventitial cells with higher bone-forming potential (Ding et al., 2019), and the highest calcification potential is attributed to mouse adventitial cells co-expressing CD34 and PDGFRα (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Human perivascular cells expressing the ROR2 Wnt receptor exhibit stronger chondrogenic ability than ROR2 negative counterparts.
source: On the other hand, human perivascular cells expressing the ROR2 Wnt receptor exhibit stronger chondrogenic ability than ROR2 negative counterparts (Dickinson et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CD146+CD107a+ human bone marrow MSCs have been described as endowed with the highest immunomodulatory and secretory, hence therapeutic, potential in experimental joint inflammation.
source: Besides, CD146+CD107a+ human bone marrow MSCs have been recently described as endowed with the highest immunomodulatory and secretory, hence therapeutic, potential in experimental joint inflammation (Bowles et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CD107a has been detected on human bone marrow and dental conventionally cultured MSCs, where it binds the enamel matrix protein amelogenin and in turn induces cell proliferation.
source: Albeit not described before at the surface of human pericytes and other perivascular cells, CD107a has been earlier detected on human bone marrow and dental conventionally cultured MSCs, where it binds the enamel matrix protein amelogenin and in turn induces cell proliferation (Huang et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Lysosomal CD107a has been linked to neural stem cell potential.
source: Besides suggested association of surface CD107a with progenitor cell proliferation and immunomodulation related tissue repair (Bowles et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2010), lysosomal CD107a has also been linked to neural stem cell potential (Yagi et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CD107a is thought to be responsible for maintaining the structural integrity of the lysosomal compartment.
source: CD107a is thought to be responsible for maintaining the structural integrity of the lysosomal compartment (Eskelinen, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Lysosomes provide the degradative enzymes for autophagy and are involved in autophagy regulation, primarily through its relationship with the master kinase complex, mTORC1.
source: Lysosomes provide the degradative enzymes for autophagy and are involved in autophagy regulation, primarily through its relationship with the master kinase complex, mTORC1 (Mrschtik and Ryan, 2015; Yim and Mizushima, 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Autophagy has been shown crucial for adipocyte differentiation.
source: Therefore, CD107a may also play an essential role in autophagy, which itself has been shown crucial for adipocyte differentiation (Guo et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: High expression of membranous CD107a, rather than having vital function in cellular differentiation, correlates with exocytosis during early adipogenic differentiation.
source: Thus, high expression of membranous CD107a, rather than having vital function in cellular differentiation, correlates with exocytosis during early adipogenic differentiation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4 and single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cell surface expression of CD107a divides osteoblast from adipocyte perivascular precursors within human tissues.
source: These results suggest that cell surface CD107a divides osteoblast from adipocyte perivascular precursors within human tissues.
